This is checking if the xyz.openbmc_project.Inventory.Item.PowerSupply interface is present in the message.

But EM does not publish that interface on either the Power_Supply_SlotX D-Bus path or the X_Configuration path.  So I'd think this would never be true.

This should be checking if either the supportedConfIntf or IBMCFFPSInterface is present, right?  Note that it should not assume both are present; they may come in different EM events.
This entire function modified

I don't think this would be true either, right?  The chassis path is the PIM path, like /xyz/openbmc_project/inventory/system/chassis2 right?

These are EM objects paths like:
* /xyz/openbmc_project/inventory/system/boardX/Foo_Backplane/Power_Supply_Slot_0
* /xyz/openbmc_project/inventory/system/chassisX/Foo/X_PSU_Configuration

The Chassis class currently has the code of how to determine if an EM path is related to the correct chassis ID.  That gets the parent object path and then looks for the Slot interface/property.

We definitely don't want to copy/paste that code, so maybe that should be moved to a chassis_utils.hpp/cpp file/namespace?  Then both the Chassis and ChassisManager could use common code to get the chassis ID associated with an EM path (if any).  Then the ChassisManager would know which Chassis to give this EM event info to.
Acknowledged

It seems like the ChassisManager knows too much and is doing too much here, on line 79, and especially on line 84.  It is treating the Chassis class more like a struct, where it knows what the data structures are and what internal methods need to get called when data changes.

The Chassis class should be more of a black box, where it has a few public methods and then calls its own internal methods.

I think lines 70, 79, and 84-88 should be inside the Chassis class.  When new PSU or PSU configuration information is added, then the Chassis class should internally call updateMissingPSUs() or restartValidationTimer() if appropriate.
Acknowledged

The ObjectMapper D-Bus interface has a GetSubTreePaths method.  It works like GetSubTree, but it only returns the paths.

The getPSUInventoryPaths() method in utility.cpp uses this.  It returns all D-Bus object paths that implement the power supply interface.

You could add a getChassisPaths() to utility.cpp that does the same thing, only with the chassis interface.

Then you could just iterate over the returned paths and create a Chassis object for each one.

This is not a requirement; just a more efficient way to do this.  Right now we are getting a bunch of additional information but only using the paths.
